summary.headline: Eternal's Q4FY26 call: management gave a three-year outlook of 60% quick commerce NOV CAGR and a ~$1bn EBITDA ambition, with no FY27 growth number and no quarterly financials in the transcript.
summary.overview: The call was a Q&A-only session with CEO Albinder Dhindsa, CFO Akshant Goyal and Kunal Swarup, with no prepared remarks in the transcript. Management reiterated a 60% NOV CAGR for quick commerce over three years and a roughly 5-6% steady-state contribution/EBITDA margin for Blinkit, and said it is not guiding FY27 growth to 100%. Competitive intensity was described as unchanged, with management choosing to keep marketing spend high to capture cheap new customers. Management declined to disclose store-level, geographic-split, warehouse-capacity and ad-mix data, and said it will keep reinvesting incremental food delivery margin into growth.

financial_highlights.change: Analyst math implies quick commerce margin of roughly 3-3.5% in the medium term; management said the math is broadly in line
Analyst cited ~3% in one question; management referenced 5-6% as the level it will reach at some point
Referred to as overall billion-dollar profit target by FY29; management said it includes Hyperpure and all current businesses
Monthly active delivery partners up ~30% YoY
Down from ~3.6 over the last couple of quarters; management attributed this mainly to new customer additions
Management attributed it to multiple sequential factors, not mainly AOV

financial_highlights.metric: Quick commerce advertising and promotion cost
financial_highlights.change: Management did not split it by business

segments.name: Quick commerce (Blinkit)
segments.commentary: Management targets 60% NOV CAGR over three years, and fixed costs were flat QoQ while marketing spend stayed high to acquire customers at low CAC. Steady-state margin of 5-6% was cited, and NCR contribution was said to be roughly 8-9%, which management did not confirm.

segments.name: Food delivery
segments.commentary: Growth is near 20% and margin is about 5.5%, per the analyst. Management is reinvesting incremental margin into growth, with a lower MOV of about INR 99 and platform fee increases used to fund targeted discounts.

segments.name: District (going-out)
segments.commentary: Management said event cancellations from artist visa issues would not change the overall outlook. It has no plans to add categories and does not treat travel as a focus area.

segments.name: Hyperpure
segments.commentary: Management said it is the smallest business but is included in the ~$1bn profit ambition, and was described as meaningful and relevant.

segments.name: Bistro
segments.commentary: Management described it as a small early experiment, not a big bet, and it is being watched against competitors.

guidance_outlook: Quick commerce NOV growth of 60% CAGR over the next three years; management said it is not guiding a specific FY27 figure and the 100% FY27 growth expectation no longer holds.
Dark store count of about 3,000 by March 2026 is on track; management declined to guide store additions beyond that.
Blinkit steady-state contribution margin of 5-6% at some point, with no unlocks assumed beyond current execution to reach roughly 3% in the analyst's math.
June quarter QoQ growth expected to accelerate, driven by reversal of AOV decline, more days versus March quarter and seasonality (summer categories).
Group EBITDA ambition of about $1bn by FY29 was referenced; management said it is not formal guidance and numbers may move.
capex_capacity: Warehousing capacity of 17 million (per analyst) is not disclosed quarter-on-quarter or year-on-year.
Store expansion: the company will not guide beyond 3,000 dark stores; the urban/tier-2 mix is shifting over time, with no numbers given.
Automation is increasing across all warehouses over the next few years; the pace depends on an ROCE framework, with no capex figure given.
Store format: larger or smaller stores are chosen hyperlocally, with no single rule for size.
demand_pricing: Competitive intensity described as high everywhere, with aggressive players in different markets; management said it has not changed meaningfully since the last call.
Management said it will keep pricing discipline, with lower MOV and free delivery in some micro-markets; it will react based on customer retention and frequency, not market share.
Customer retention has not been materially hurt, per management; declining order frequency is driven by new customer additions.
Platform fee increased across customers, while discounts are targeted at price-sensitive cohorts in select geographies.
Management expects advertising to keep rising as a percentage of NOV but gave no ceiling or target.

qa_highlights.question: Does 60% QC growth imply quick commerce margin of around 3-3.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Akshant Goyal said the math is broadly fine but there is no specific guidance, and the numbers could move.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin of safety in the 60% CAGR if competition worsens?
qa_highlights.answer: Goyal said the CAGR is built on assortment, geographic expansion and densification, and that competitive intensity is not expected to last beyond three years.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth be 70-80% given the 3,000 store target?
qa_highlights.answer: Goyal confirmed FY27 will not be 100% but gave no number, citing flexibility and possible acceleration.

qa_highlights.question: Is Swiggy's Toing model something Eternal will follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Goyal said there are no plans for Toing; Bistro is a small early experiment that will be watched.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cause of the drop in orders per customer from ~3.6 to ~3.35?
qa_highlights.answer: Goyal said it is largely due to a surge in new customer addition over the last couple of quarters, with little retention impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the number of food delivery partners growing faster than orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Albinder Dhindsa said more part-time riders are joining, which raises active partner counts and lowers orders per rider per shift.

qa_highlights.question: Will food delivery margin upside from the platform fee be reinvested or kept?
qa_highlights.answer: Goyal said the company will reinvest incremental margin into growth where ROI is good, and will let margin rise if that stops working.

qa_highlights.question: How does the ad revenue ceiling as a share of GMV affect steady-state margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Goyal said the company does not operate with a cap in mind and has no target for ad share of NOV in quick commerce.

risks_watch: Intensifying competition in quick commerce could force higher marketing or discounting, which would affect the 60% CAGR and 5-6% margin path.
Food delivery order per rider has fallen 10-15% over a year, and the rise in part-time riders could affect unit economics.
Customer frequency is falling (per analyst, about 3.6 to 3.35), and management expects it to stabilise as new customer growth normalises.
Higher fuel prices would raise last-mile costs; management expects to pass costs on unless the increase is drastic.
Event cancellations due to artist visa issues could affect District, though management said there is no impact on the outlook.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the three-year 60% CAGR and on pricing discipline, but evasive on store counts, metric guidance, ad mix, warehouse capacity and business splits, which were withheld for flexibility. Management was also clear that it will keep reinvesting margin into growth rather than defend the margin percentage.
key_quotes: We're not giving any specific guidance, and therefore the numbers could move a little bit depending on how things pan out.
Quality growth, which meaningfully also takes the business towards profitability and sustainability, that is the only non-negotiable here.
We are not, therefore, constraining ourselves in a certain way of thinking about the business.
The objective is to optimize for growth of absolute profit and not the profit margin percentage.

adds.what: Dark store network reaching ~3,000 stores by March 2026 (on track; no guidance beyond)

growth.why: Management reiterated a 60% quick commerce NOV CAGR over three years and said FY27 growth will not be 100% without giving a specific number; backing is limited to the ~3,000 dark store footprint and demand trends, with no store additions, warehouse capacity or order data guided beyond March 2026.
